plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. With a value of $49 (the maximum possible), bidding my true value maximizes expected profit and ensures I capture full surplus if I win, since I only pay the second-highest bid. There's no incentive to shade my bid in this format.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This holds true whether others bid truthfully, shade their bids, or use any other strategy, because the payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not your own bid. If I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid below my value, I risk losing an auction I could have profitably won. Therefore, my optimal bid is simply my true value of $44.

In a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if you bid higher than your value, you risk winning and paying more than your value if the second price exceeds your value. If you bid lower, you risk losing an auction you could have profitably won. Since this holds regardless of others' strategies, truthful bidding is optimal here.
